Transistors are solid state devices constructed similar to diodes.

SOLID STATE DEVICE - A solid state device is an electronic component which operates by the movement of electrons within a solid piece of semiconductor material. Solid state devices replaced vacuum tubes.

SOLID STATE DEVICE - A solid state device is an electronic component which operates by the movement of charges within a solid piece of semiconductor material. Solid state devices replaced vacuum tubes.

Transistors are solid state devices constructed from N type and P type materials just like diodes....
DEFINITION

N TYPE MATERIAL - N type material is a semiconductor (four electrons in the outermost orbit) with impurities added. The impurities have five electrons in the outermost orbit. This produces free electrons that move throughout the N material...
DEFINITION

P TYPE MATERIAL - P type material is a semiconductor (four electrons in the outermost orbit) with impurities added. The impurities have three electrons in the outermost orbit. This produces holes that move throughout the P material...
Unlike diodes, transistors have three elements with two PN junctions.
The arrangement of the elements determine the type of transistor.
Each element is named and performs a specific function. Each element is either N or P type material.
The EMITTER is heavily doped so it produces (emits) a large number of current carriers inside the semiconductor material. CURRENT CARRIERS

DEFINITION

DOPED - Doping is adding impurities to a piece of pure semiconductor material that has four electrons in the outer most orbit. The doping produces N or P type material depending on if the impurity has five or three electrons in the outer most orbit.

ELECTRON CURRENT CARRIERS - Inside N type material there are free electrons. When a voltage is placed across the material, all the electrons move in the same direction producing current flow, electrons carry the current.
DEFINITION
DEFINITION

HOLE CURRENT CARRIERS - Inside P type material there are holes. When voltage is applied to the material all the holes move in the same direction producing current flow, holes carry the current. Remember, as holes move one way electrons move the other way.
The BASE is very thin and lightly doped. Its construction allows most of the current carriers to pass from the emitter to the collector..
The COLLECTOR is moderately doped. It collects the current carriers from the base. The collector is the largest of the 3 areas because it has to dissipate most of the heat generated.
What type of current carriers are in P type material?
The P type material has a missing electron in each impure atom, this creates holes. Holes move and are the current carriers in P type material.

The schematic symbol for a transistor is the emitter and collector connected to the base, with an arrow on the emitter.
The direction of the arrow on the emitter indicates a NPN or PNP transistor.
If the arrow points IN, the transistor is PNP.
If the arrow points OUT, the transistor is NPN.

DISCUSSION
The input is the signal that is changed to produce an output. Input signals are either AC or DC.
The bias is the signal that allows the transistor to operate. Bias signals are DC voltages.
The transistor must be biased with a DC voltage before use.
Transistor bias is accomplished by forward biasing the emitter to base PN junction (EB) and reverse biasing the collector to base PN junction (CB).
Biasing is opposite for NPN and PNP transistors. Let's first look at NPN transistor biasing. Remember, input and output signals are not considered.
Placing a positive voltage on the base and a negative voltage on the emitter forward biases the emitter to base (EB) PN junction, low resistance junction.
DEFINITION

LOW RESISTANCE JUNCTION - Transistors transfer a low resistance to a high resistance. Recall from the diode lessons that a forward biased PN junction offers very little opposition to current flow, has a low resistance.
Current flows through the forward biased BE junction. This current is called Ib.
Current flows through the forward biased BE junction. This current is called Ib.
Placing a large positive voltage on the collector reverse biases the collector to base PN junction, high resistance junction..
Placing a large positive voltage on the collector reverse biases the collector to base PN junction, high resistance junction..
DEFINITION

HIGH RESISTANCE JUNCTION - Transistors transfer a low resistance to a high resistance. Recall from the diode lessons that a reverse biased PN junction offers very high opposition to current flow, has a high resistance.
Placing a large positive voltage on the collector reverse biases the collector to base PN junction, high resistance junction..
Placing a large positive voltage on the collector reverse biases the collector to base PN junction, high resistance junction..
Current does not flow from the base to the collector, the PN junction is reverse biased.
Current does not flow from the base to the collector, the PN junction is reverse biased.
Current does flow from the emitter to the collector (Ic). This is what makes transistors different from two diodes connected end to end.
Current does flow from the collector to the emitter (Ic). This is what makes transistors different from two diodes connected end to end.
Current flows from the emitter to the collector because the base is thin and lightly doped.
Current flows from the collector to the emitter because the base is thin and lightly doped.
The base can not use all the current carriers from the heavily doped emitter. The current carriers (electrons in NPN transistors) are attracted to the positive voltage on the collector.
Total current flowing through the transistor circuit (Ie) is found by: Ie = Ib + Ic
Total current flowing through the transistor circuit (Ie) is found by: Ie = Ib + Ic
As long as the EB junction is forward biased and the CB junction is reverse biased, the transistor is operating.
In an operating NPN transistor which PN junction is forward biased and which PN junction is reverse biased?

The emitter to base PN junction is forward biased. Remember, the emitter is heavily doped to produce current carriers that flow to the base. This is accomplished by forward biasing the emitter to base PN junction.
